newsitem.title: GERMANY: ADIDAS CEO SEES MORE DOUBLE-DIGIT GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: ADIDAS CEO SEES MORE DOUBLE-DIGIT GROWTH.

text.p: Adidas AG chief executive Robert Louis-Dreyfus said on Tuesday that he expected the German sportswear maker to keep up its pace of reporting double-digit profit growth in the coming years.

"I think the trend is that we will grow at double-digit rates, over 20 percent but not above 50 percent," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview after the group's annual news conference.
He said Adidas would concentrate on the Far East, which he said was a "fantastic growth area" but also increase advertising and promotion spending in the United States.
Adidas earlier on Tuesday said pre-tax income rose 50 percent to 444 million marks (260.7 million) as net sales rose 35 percent to a record high of 4.7 billion marks (2.8 billion).
Louis-Dreyfus said Europe currently accounts for 57 percent of Adidas's global sales but would like that level to fall to less than 50 percent by the turn of the century.
He said the goal was for North America to account for about 25 percent of worldwide sales in 2000 and for the rest of the world to account for the remaining balance.
